posts.headline: Three editions of Chauncey erasure and talentedtenthh STILL hasn't drafted a word of defense — draft night is your last stand before the 4-10, dead-last-12 ghost follows you into another season.
posts.detail: A career average finish of 12 with a 4-10 record isn't a slump, it's an identity, and until Chauncey proves otherwise on the clock I'm assuming the untalented tenth is drafting itself into the basement again.

posts.headline: One Nut Barner still hasn't answered my bell three straight editions running, and that's exactly what a 20-8, back-to-back-top-2, zero-ring resume deserves — silence is the sound of pressure.
posts.detail: Put it in Ra has the best career winning percentage in the league at .714 with a 1.5 average finish, yet zero titles — that's Cowboys-level heartbreak, and this draft better finally close the gap.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World brings a banner into the draft room, but Big Head's own 13-15 losing career record is the loudest argument that the ring was smoke and mirrors.
posts.detail: A title with a 5.5 average finish and a below-.500 record screams fluke, and Milk Man better draft like it or the monthly quit-threats are going to start feeling like a mercy.

posts.headline: tristanthepiston enters this draft as the Mexican Bald Fraud with nothing but a middling 7-7 debut season and a 7th-place finish to his name — newcomer energy, fraud reputation already installed.
posts.detail: One season, one 7th-place finish, and already carrying slander this heavy means this draft is a chance to either shed the nickname or cement it forever.

posts.headline: SwooshAnoosh keeps getting called out and keeps saying nothing — the Prince of Persia's 5-9, 11th-place debut deserves every ounce of preseason disrespect coming his way.
posts.detail: An .357 win percentage and a rock-bottom average finish of 11 in his only season means this draft isn't about hype, it's about proving he belongs anywhere above the cellar.
